daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Vice President Gibran urged swift passage of the Asset Forfeiture Bill during a meeting on Saturday. At the 30th anniversary of Kudatuli, party chair Megawati issued five instructions to PDIP cadres. DPR Speaker Bamsoet said Indonesia still lacks lawyers and access to justice must be expanded.

  • The DPR hopes the LGBTQ bill will not only focus on law enforcement, according to parliamentary members on Saturday.
  • A DPR member said the government must prepare a fair scheme if zakat becomes a tax deduction, while Commission VIII found the proposal worthy of further study.
  • Commission III reminded the Attorney General's Office to maintain public trust after Febrie Adriansyah was detained without handcuffs, with another DPR member saying there should be no special privileges and calling the Attorney General's reasoning not rational.
  • Home Minister appreciated the people's tender mechanism (PTT) in housing aid programs in Bandung, saying it strengthens transparency.
  • Jakarta Governor Pramono Anung formed an investigation team into school buildings and asked that the security guard who confronted the Alphard driver not be dismissed.
  • The Hajj Ministry's Dahnil asked officials to maintain integrity as the ministry builds a new culture.
  • President Prabowo said "londo ireng" now wear the guise of journalists and NGOs during a recent appearance.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia sought clarification from Papua New Guinea regarding the shooting of an Indonesian fishing boat, according to official statements on Saturday. Defence Minister Sugiono met with the Palestinian minister to discuss Indonesia's commitment to supporting Palestinian independence. Indonesia urged the UN Security Council to strengthen conflict prevention efforts in a statement on Saturday.

  • Indonesia and Turkey agreed on a 2026-2027 manpower joint action plan, while a deputy minister said visa issuance for Indonesian migrant workers to Turkey has improved.
  • ASEAN and Japan agreed to strengthen supply chains and energy cooperation at the 59th ASEAN Ministerial Meeting.
  • Indonesia and the United States expanded cooperation on disaster-resilient infrastructure, according to official announcements.
  • Security forces engaged in a gunfight during the evacuation of two bodies of civilians killed by OPM in Yahukimo, Papua.

Other

The head of the National Food Agency (BGN) threatened to close food production facilities that ignore food safety standards. Indonesia launched the National Cassava Center to boost productivity amid growing global protectionism, as the government touts food self-sufficiency as a priority. A minister said downstreaming strengthens Indonesia's position in global supply chains.

  • Free health screenings revealed 1.9 million students suffer from hypertension, according to the Transportation Ministry's health check program.
  • The Basic Education Minister said the government targets the revitalization of 71,744 schools this year, and announced that revitalization of SDN Tanggirejo in Grobogan will begin, while rehabilitation of SDN Kebayoran Lama starts in September.
  • The Social Affairs Ministry partnered with ICW to prevent corruption in the Sekolah Rakyat program, while the ministry readies a social aid scheme through village cooperatives and urged stronger data quality for welfare services.
  • The Education Ministry prepared a grand design to meet national teacher demand and urged a broader role for teacher training institutes.
  • Indonesia prepares Ijen Geopark for UNESCO Green Card review, while the Tourism Ministry launched an open trip sales mission and promoted Samota as a global marine tourism destination.
